Style and housekeeping:

Records API redesign

Make the record writes data-first and type-stable, modelled on dplyr’s rows_*(): the first argument is the thing the function returns, so a data frame can be piped in and comes back. grist_resolve_refs() already works this way. Schema, read and document functions stay doc-first. Do this as one pass that also updates the README, vignettes, examples and tests, and run the live tests.

Booleans to review

Prefer an enum to a flag (design guide) when an argument can plausibly take more values or only makes sense with another argument.

  • overwrite and parse are probably fine as logicals. hidden, raw, pinned and enabled are plain on/off switches.

Out of scope

These stay reachable through grist_request(): SCIM and user admin, access rules, proposals, POST /docs/{id}/apply (raw user actions), archive attachment endpoints, document recovery and force-reload, and copying a document (sourceDocumentId, asTemplate).

Known limitations

  • An empty Bool cell reads back as FALSE (Grist behaviour). It’s documented.
  • grist_resolve_refs() makes one extra request per referenced table.
  • Formula columns are exported as values, not formulas.
  • grist_import() leaves created tables and rows in place if a request fails part way.
  • grist_doc(api_key = 1) errors, but the message names grist_request_options() rather than grist_doc().

Dependencies to watch

  • S7 is pre-1.0 (developed against 0.2.2.9000), and the minimum R is 4.2.
  • data-dict is at spec version 0.1.0. It doesn’t allow extension keys and forbids foreign keys on list columns, which is why grist_import() takes a types argument. Revisit if the spec changes.
